title: EPFO Extends September PF Filing Deadline to October 31
excerpt: Employers get 16 extra days to file September 2026 PF returns after the wage ceiling rose mid-month to Rs 25,000. Employees should verify their passbook once credits land.
body:
• EPFO has extended the deadline for filing September 2026 PF returns and depositing contributions from October 15 to October 31, 2026 — 16 extra days.
  • The extension applies only to the September 2026 wage month. It follows the PF wage ceiling rising from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 a month, effective September 17.
  • Filing is your employer's job, not yours: employees do not file the ECR themselves.
  • What employees should do: check the EPF passbook after filing, verify September salary and contribution records, and raise missing credits with HR or payroll.

India's Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO) has given employers until October 31, 2026 to file provident fund returns and deposit contributions for September — moving a deadline that had already fallen due on October 15. The extension, issued in a circular dated October 13, covers the Electronic Challan-cum-Return (ECR) and the remittance of statutory contributions for the September 2026 wage month only, SCC Times reports.

Why the deadline moved

The trigger was a mid-month rule change. The statutory wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage rose from Rs 15,000 to Rs 25,000 per month, effective September 17, 2026 — in the middle of the September payroll cycle. Employers told EPFO they faced technical, operational and administrative difficulties recalculating employee-wise contributions and reconfiguring payroll systems at short notice. EPFO granted the extension under Paragraph 28(3) of the Employees' Provident Funds Scheme, 1952, to allow payroll updates and accurate compliance, according to the circular summary published by CA Club India.

https://x.com/livemint/status/2110745376680726905

The filing covers contributions under three heads: the Employees' Provident Fund (EPF), the Employees' Pension Scheme (EPS) and the Employees' Deposit Linked Insurance (EDLI) scheme. The relief is narrow by design — EPFO has clarified it is not a general extension for other wage months and does not waive any other obligation.

What employees should check

Employees do not file anything themselves; the ECR is an employer compliance requirement. The employee's job is verification, and SightsIn Plus sets out the checks. Once the employer files and pays, review your EPF passbook to confirm the September contribution is credited. Check that the salary and contribution figures match your pay slip and the revised wage-ceiling rules. If a credit is missing after the filing and payment process completes, contact your payroll or HR team, and ask the employer to explain any discrepancy between the salary slip and the PF record.

What employers must do with the extra time

Payroll teams are expected to use the 16 additional days to review the impact of the revised ceiling on employee-wise calculations, update payroll configurations and reconcile contributions before filing. The extension moves the date; it does not reduce the obligation. Establishments that miss October 31 for the September wage month are outside the relief the circular grants.

For NRI readers

Anyone who worked in India and still holds an EPF account — including NRIs who have not yet withdrawn or transferred their balance — is affected the same way: your former or current employer's September credit may land later than usual because of this extension. Check the passbook after October 31 before assuming a contribution is missing, and raise discrepancies with the employer's payroll team first.
